review_workflow.description: Nothing auto-posts. Every run renders the week and writes it to output/queue/ with an HTML preview. Dave reviews once a week, edits if needed, then approves by running scripts/push-queue.js, which hands the approved week to Buffer for scheduled posting at each slot's time.
review_workflow.generation_note: Run the weekly pipeline on Thursday for the FOLLOWING week. This gives a relaxed Thu-Sun review window instead of a rushed same-day approval.
review_workflow.posts_go_live: The following week at each slot's scheduled time
review_workflow.october_note: In October (daily), one weekly review covers all 7 posts at once - generate a week ahead and batch-approve.

_schedule_logic: Weekdays = community/relationship content (humor, motivation, engagement, mission) to grow reach when engagement is highest. Weekends = product/commerce content, when the audience has time and intent to actually shop. Times are tuned to the trades audience: early lunch, after-work evening, relaxed weekend browsing.

base_week.description: Default cadence: 4 posts + 2 reels per week (6x). Reels are the Mon and Thu slots; the reel theme rotates motivational/mission/product (reel_content_rotation) and the visual style rotates weekly (reel_styles). Active Jan-Aug (chosen by calendar month); posting times come straight from each slot's `time` below — Miley does NOT use a POST_SCHEDULE env var (that's Milly/Molly).

slots.rationale: Monday-evening reel to open the week. Reel theme comes from reel_content_rotation (motivational/mission/product), not the community pool.
Lunch scroll. Tradeswomen take early lunch; Tuesday afternoon is a strong, reliable engagement window.
Thursday evening has a confirmed 2026 engagement spike and is the best window for Reels (after-work wind-down).
Friday lunch community post (humor/motivation/engagement) to keep reach up heading into the weekend.
Saturday late-morning = relaxed, high-INTENT browsing. Engagement is lower than midweek, but buying intent is higher. This is the money slot.
Sunday early evening is the wind-down + week-planning window. Good for a softer product/mission combo.

september_ramp.description: Activated Sept 1. Adds a Wednesday post on top of the 6x base (→ 7x/week) to build audience momentum heading into October.

added_slot.rationale: Wednesday noon is the single highest-engagement slot of the week. Use it to seed breast cancer awareness storytelling before October.

october_daily.description: Activated Oct 1. Daily posting for Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Full schedule and content mix live in october-campaign.json.

weekday_community.rotation_note: Advance one step per post using current_week modulo rotation length. Humor and motivation should appear most often; mission roughly every 4th community post so it never feels preachy.

product.rotation_note: Rotate which product is featured across the 8-product catalog so no single item dominates. Lifestyle = a person wearing/using the product; social_proof = review/order-screenshot style once real sales exist.

product_mission.rotation_note: Alternates a straight lifestyle product shot with a product post that leans harder on the 30% donation angle.

mission_buildup.rotation_note: September-only pool to warm the audience toward October. awareness_stat uses real data from inspiration-sources.json.

_reel_styles_note: Weekly A/B rotation for reel visual style (planner picks styleList[current_week % len], uniform across the week). card = beat-card motion; kinetic_karaoke = words reveal progressively with the active word highlighted; kinetic_punch = one big word at a time. Trim this list to run a 2-way test (e.g. ["card","kinetic_karaoke"]).
_reel_content_note: What reels are ABOUT (separate from visual style). A reel slot cycles its theme through this list across reel weeks instead of using the weekday community pool. product_feature_lifestyle pulls a product and uses its photo background when assets/products/<key>.png exists. Reorder or trim to change the mix (e.g. drop products, or add "trades_humor").

_meta.note: current_week is a single incrementing counter advanced once per pipeline run. Adding/removing items from any rotation array requires no code change. Cadence (base -> september -> october) switches AUTOMATICALLY by calendar month (planner.getCampaignMode). Base/September posting times come straight from each slot's `time`; only October parses `october_daily.post_schedule_env`. The base/september `post_schedule_env` strings are reference-only — Miley does NOT read a POST_SCHEDULE env var (unlike Milly/Molly, whose file this mirrors).
